_note: The module-identity CHAIN corpus (facet-contracts.md, derived identity). THE LAW: a module's identity is its dotted chain derived from Modules/ nesting (a manifest declares only its LOCAL segment); segments are [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, depth <= 4; the chain is BOTH the API face (dsx.module.watch.health.heartRate) and the wire scheme token (watch.health://heartRate). RESOLUTION is the incremental FOLD at each runtime's ONE dispatch funnel — never dot-counting, never a first-dot split: (1) normalize the arriving HEAD spelling through the alias map to its primary chain (watchhealth -> watch.health; an unknown head stays itself, known=false — module_not_found reports against the head token, never a silent no-op); (2) while the remaining action path is non-empty and chain + '.' + parts[0] is in the IDENTITY SET (registered chains UNION build-excluded chains — the honest universe, so an excluded child still gets correct attribution instead of becoming a phantom action on its parent), fold that segment into the chain; (3) what remains is the action path (slash-joined here, the native array-path convention; empty = the bare pre-filter call). The build-time bidirectional ban (a child segment can never equal a parent action/group first-segment or a reserved member — dsx_graph chain_errors) is what makes the fold total and unambiguous: intelligence.rag.add can only ever mean the rag GROUP because a child named rag could not have built. Aliases are consulted at HEAD position only and keep legacy grammar (hyphens fine — they route wire tokens and window.despia, never the modern dot plane); the arriving spelling stays visible to the module (ctx.scheme — catch-all routing) while identity (state, events, config) is always the primary chain. RESERVED MEMBERS { on, available, excluded, state, context, object, delegate, dsx, then } are never actions: after the fold, a leading reserved word in the remainder routes to the MEMBER plane (kind 'member' below) — the call parser refuses it as an action. PROXY SAFETY (the JS planes): a property get of then / toString / valueOf / toJSON / constructor / __proto__ or any Symbol on a module or member proxy returns undefined — await never half-calls a proxy, JSON.stringify and console.log never fire a phantom call; native proxies are immune by construction (reserved members are REAL members, and real members shadow dynamic lookup — SE-0195 — which is also why this set is CLOSED and FROZEN: growth is a major-version event). A reserved member that nevertheless arrives at a MODERN call face — the typed proxies, the dotted-callee face, the native _call/_dispatch funnel (impossible through the proxies themselves, i.e. a caller bug) — is REFUSED with the error code `reserved_member` (reported through module.callFailed, thrown as the runtime's ModuleCallError), the same spelling on every runtime. The LEGACY WIRE face (URL navigations, the v3 string transport) is EXEMPT from the refusal and routes DIRECT: reserved words are banned from MANIFESTS, never from the wire, so a code-only legacy shim registered under a reserved spelling (biometric://available, bluetooth://state, scanningmode://on) keeps answering shipped pages — the compat those shims exist for. On the wire face the FOLD still applies for ROUTING — a nested chain reaches its owner even when the remainder starts with a reserved word (chfx://sub/state dispatches action 'state' on chfx.sub, where a shim answers and an unregistered name answers unknown_action) — so the owner and the attribution are the same on every runtime; only the refusal is face-gated. Runners: TS (vitest) and Kotlin (:core JUnit) execute every case; Swift is the reference (record lane). Case shape: input = the dotted callee after 'dsx.module.' (a lone token = the bare scheme-only call); expect.chain = the resolved primary identity; expect.action = the slash-joined remainder ('' = bare); expect.member/rest instead of action for member-plane routes; expect.spelling = the arriving head when it differs from the chain (alias calls); expect.known=false marks an unresolvable head; expect.excluded=true marks identity resolved through the excluded overlay.

proxySafety._note: JS-plane runners (TS kernel proxy, runtime.js window.dsx/window.despia proxies) assert for every denylisted name AND for Symbol keys: a property get returns undefined (never a callable proxy), so `await proxy` resolves the proxy itself, JSON.stringify(proxy) treats it as a plain function value, and console/inspect never dispatch. Kotlin and Swift skip this block (no dynamic get plane — reserved members are real members).
